title: Cloned Voices and Faces
about: How AI copies voices and faces, and why permission matters.

cards.prompt: AI can fake a real person's **voice** or **video**. Is each use **helpful** or **harmful**?

items.label: Dubbing a film, with the actors' OK
Giving back a voice someone lost
A museum guide in 10 languages, with OK
A fake call that sounds like Grandma
A fake video to embarrass a classmate
A fake singer advert selling a product

cards.hint: Ask: does everyone in it know and agree, and is anyone being tricked?
cards.nudge: Look for whether everyone agreed, and whether someone is fooled.
cards.explanation: Dubbing with consent, restoring a lost voice and the museum guide **help**, and nobody's fooled. A fake Grandma call, an embarrassing video and a fake advert **trick or hurt** people.

cards.title: Fake faces and voices
cards.body:
A fake video or picture of a real person is a **deepfake**; a **voice clone** copies their voice. Most tools learn from many voices, then copy one from a short clip.

In Australia, sharing fake sexual images of a real person without their consent is a serious crime, and fake sexual images of anyone under 18 are always illegal.

cards.prompt: Why can a [[voice clone|voice-clone]] sometimes be made from just a short clip of someone talking?

options.text: It can only replay the exact words in the clip
options.nudge: A clone can say new words the person never said. So what does it already know?

options.text: It already learned how voices work from many people
It stitches words from the clip into new sentences
options.nudge: Clones can say words that aren't in the clip. What does the model already know?

options.text: Short clips hold more voice detail than long ones
options.nudge: Longer recordings usually help. Why might a short one still be enough?

cards.hint: Before it ever hears this person, what has the model already learned from?
cards.explanation: Trained on **many voices**, it already knows how voices work, so a short clip only shows what's special about **this** voice. Worth remembering before you post your voice publicly.

cards.prompt: Your friend found a face-swap app. Faking a real person without **permission** can hurt them and spread far.

steps.text: "Let's make a video of our coach dancing badly and saying silly things. It's just a joke!" What do you say?

choices.text: "Only if we put 'FAKE' in tiny letters at the end"
choices.consequence: Your coach never agreed, and a tiny label is easy to miss or crop off. It can still spread and hurt them.

choices.text: "OK, but we'll only send it to two friends"
choices.consequence: Two friends can share it with anyone. You can't control a video once it's sent.

choices.text: "No: they haven't agreed, and it could hurt them"
choices.consequence: Right. Without permission, it isn't a joke, it's a fake of a real person.

cards.hint: Who has to agree first? Does a label or a small audience change that?
cards.explanation: Without the coach's **permission**, it's a deepfake of a real person, label or not, and anything sent can spread. In Australia, sharing fake sexual images of a real person without their consent is a serious crime, and fake sexual images of anyone under 18 are always illegal.

cards.prompt: Clues can be **in the video** or **in the situation**, which often tells more. Best check: the real person, another way.

items.label: Lips don't quite match the words
The voice sounds flat and odd
The edge of the face flickers
Posted by an account you don't know
No one else is reporting it

cards.hint: Could you spot it by watching closely, or by asking where it came from?
cards.nudge: Which could you only spot by watching the face and listening closely?
cards.explanation: Lip-sync, odd voices and flickering edges are **in the video**. Who posted it, a rush and whether anyone else reports it are **in the situation**, and often the stronger clues.

cards.prompt: A video shows a famous singer: "1,000 free concert tickets! Click the link in the next hour."

steps.text: It looks and sounds just like them, on a page you've never seen. What do you do?

choices.text: Click the link quickly before the tickets go
choices.consequence: The rush is the trick: the link asks for your card details. It was a deepfake advert.

choices.text: Watch closely to check the lips match the words
choices.consequence: The lips match perfectly: good fakes pass that test. The situation is the stronger clue.

choices.text: Check the singer's official account for the news
choices.consequence: Their official account says nothing about it, and warns of fake giveaway videos. It was a deepfake.

cards.hint: Spot the situation clues first, then think about the best check.
cards.explanation: An unknown page, a rush and "free" are **situation clues**. Faces and voices can be faked, so check the **real person's official account** or trusted news.

cards.prompt: Your uncle gets an upset call that sounds just like you, asking for money fast. What's **best** for him to do?

options.text: Hang up, then call you on the number he already has
Listen closely for a flat or robotic voice first
options.nudge: A good clone can sound perfect. Which check doesn't rely on this call?

options.text: Send a small amount first, to see if it's really you
options.nudge: Money sent to a faker is gone. How could he check without paying?

options.text: Ask the caller to say his name, to prove it's you
options.nudge: Whoever called knows his name. Which check goes outside this call?

cards.hint: The voice can be faked. Which check doesn't go through this call?
cards.explanation: **Call back on a number he already has**: that check goes another way, so a faker can't answer it. Clones can sound perfect, and money sent to a scammer is usually gone.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- AI can fake a real person: **deepfakes** and **voice clones**.
- Never fake a real person without their permission.
- Situation clues beat video clues: check with the real person.

If someone fakes **you**, it's not your fault. Report it at esafety.gov.au, and tell a trusted adult. More in Stay Safe Online's free lesson **Deepfake Scams and Fakes**.
